points.why: Names Fixes That Fail and explains that each sign-off works short term while its side effect, bundling into bigger releases, makes incidents riskier and harder to diagnose, which in turn prompts more sign-offs.
Traces the side-effect chain well but merges it with the quick fix into one reinforcing loop, never identifies the balancing loop, and doesn't mention the months-long delay.
Calls the draft action item the third turn of the loop, but never asks what a fourth sign-off would do a few rounds later.

Recommends small, frequent deploys, automated checks, feature flags and fast rollback, and tracking changes per deploy and time-to-identify-cause; it doesn't explicitly frame any extra review as a stopgap.
Frames the write-up around the pattern across incidents and the structure, but never names the underlying belief that more approval means more safety.

pitfalls.why: Explicitly advises against the fourth sign-off and allows only a risk-proportional review for migrations.
Does not blame any individual engineer.

notes: The claim that 'every link is positive, so it reinforces itself' is wrong for the quick-fix link, which reduces incidents and forms a balancing loop.
